label: Camoufox (stealth Firefox)
requirements: uv (pinned 0.13.5): an explicit UV/UV_BIN or a working uv on PATH is used, otherwise the pinned release is downloaded into the plugin data directory and SHA-256 verified
Plugin-managed CPython 3.13.17 (installed by uv under the plugin data directory; UV_PYTHON or PYTHON override)

camoufox-playwright-mcp==0.1.5 plus its Python MCP stack fastmcp==3.4.7 and mcp==1.29.0 (installed into <plugin data>/venvs/camoufox on first start; CAMOUFOX_MCP_PACKAGE overrides the wrapper pin only). The stack is pinned to the wrapper's own uv.lock because its pyproject.toml declares fastmcp>=3.4.2 with no upper bound: fastmcp 4.x serves the 2026-07-28 protocol era, where each request gets a new session id and the wrapper relaunches the browser on every tool call
Camoufox build v156.0.1-beta.39 (one-time ~1.3 GB download, ~2.4 GB on disk)

toolSupportNotes.browser_annotate: Not implemented by camoufox-playwright-mcp 0.1.5; it omits the upstream Node dashboard daemon.
toolSupportNotes.browser_emulate_media: Not implemented by camoufox-playwright-mcp 0.1.5; absent from its tool registry.
toolSupportNotes.browser_start_recording: Not implemented by camoufox-playwright-mcp 0.1.5; absent from its tool registry.
toolSupportNotes.browser_stop_recording: Not implemented by camoufox-playwright-mcp 0.1.5; absent from its tool registry.
toolSupportNotes.browser_pdf_save: Listed by the backend but unusable on Firefox: PDF output is only supported by headless Chromium.
toolSupportNotes.browser_run_code_unsafe: Executes asynchronous Python Playwright code, not JavaScript; a prompt written for the JS tool will fail.

notes: Stealth Firefox via camoufox-playwright-mcp 0.1.5. 68 of the 72 canonical browser tools; portable by default. Needs no system Python or uv: the launcher provisions a pinned uv, a managed Python and a venv under the plugin data directory on first start. No CDP. The venv pins the Python MCP stack (fastmcp==3.4.7, mcp==1.29.0) to the wrapper's uv.lock; without that pin fastmcp 4.x answers in the 2026-07-28 protocol era, whose per-request session id makes the wrapper start a new browser on every tool call. Revisit the pin when upstream bounds fastmcp itself or keys its browser backend by a stable id. Before starting, the broker checks Firefox's own parent.lock in the profile and refuses a profile a live browser already holds, instead of hanging or failing the first launch; a leftover lock from an exited browser is reported as stale and does not block. The wrapper's own server heartbeat is off by default: it pings every 3 s and closes the browser when an answer is more than 5 s late, and one late client answer was enough to end a session, so the ping_timeout_ms setting defaults to 0 and a positive value re-enables the heartbeat with that deadline (an explicit PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS overrides it); browser_capabilities and browser_engine_status report pingTimeoutMs, pingTimeoutSource and heartbeatEnabled.
